*   **Precision**: The choice of `MortonType` (16-bit vs 32-bit) limits the maximum spatial extent and affects performance [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the `rapid_svo::tree` is templated on `MortonType` (which can be 16-bit or 32-bit based on the dependency `libmorton` and benchmark labels like `16b_space` and `32b_space`). The benchmarks show that changing the Morton type (and associated grid size/bounds) results in significantly different performance metrics (e.g., alloc speed drops from ~58M vox/s to ~30M vox/s when moving from 16b/16^3 to 32b/128^3). Furthermore, the evidence mentions `_limit_max_bounds` and `_discard_overflow`, indicating that the choice of type and configuration limits the spatial extent. Thus, the claim that the choice of MortonType limits spatial extent and affects performance is fully supported by the provided text and data.
